prop:jet-prolongation:
Proposition Jet Prolongation. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe over a ring R (quantum observable universe). Assume A is commutative, and let \Omega^1_{A/R} = I/I^2, I = \ker(m \colon A \otimes A \to A), be the module of Kähler differentials, the complement of A in the jet object J^1(A) = (A \otimes A)/I^2. One defines the tangent algebra

  T(A) := \mathrm{Sym}_A\bigl(\Omega^1_{A/R}\bigr).

Its degree-\le 1 truncation is J^1(A) = A \oplus \Omega^1_{A/R}. The structure map \ell \colon A \to T(A) and the augmentation r \colon T(A) \to A, which kills \Omega^1_{A/R}, satisfy r \circ \ell = \mathrm{id}_A. When A = \mathcal{O}(G) is the coordinate Hopf algebra of an affine group G, T(A) = \mathcal{O}(TG) is the coordinate Hopf algebra of the tangent group TG = G \ltimes \mathrm{Lie}(G), and \ell and r are Hopf maps: the pull-backs along the projection TG \to G and along the zero section. At the tower levels n \ge 1 only this Hopf structure and the splitting are required. No Frobenius form on T(A) is required, and (\mathbf{C}, T(A), \tau', q) is not claimed to be a quantum observable universe: in characteristic zero \mathcal{O}(TG) has no nonzero integral, since TG contains the vector group \mathrm{Lie}(G).
ex:jet-prolongation-su2:
Example Jet prolongation of \mathcal{O}(\mathrm{SU}(2)). One explicitly constructs the jet prolongation of A = \mathcal{O}(\mathrm{SU}(2)).

Kähler differentials. Let I = \ker(m \colon A \otimes A \to A). The module of Kähler differentials is \Omega^1_A = I/I^2. Since \mathrm{SU}(2) is a smooth group of dimension 3, it is free with a left-invariant basis:

  \Omega^1_A = \mathrm{span}_A\{\omega_1, \omega_2, \omega_3\},

where \omega_a are the left-invariant 1-forms dual to the Lie algebra basis \{e_1, e_2, e_3\} of \mathfrak{su}(2).

The tangent algebra. By definition:

  T(A) := \mathrm{Sym}_A(\Omega^1_A) = A[\omega_1, \omega_2, \omega_3],

the polynomial algebra over A in the three left-invariant forms. It is the coordinate algebra \mathcal{O}(T\,\mathrm{SU}(2)) of the tangent group T\,\mathrm{SU}(2) \cong \mathrm{SU}(2) \ltimes \mathfrak{su}(2). The structure map A \to T(A) and the augmentation T(A) \to A, \omega_a \mapsto 0, satisfy r \circ \ell = \mathrm{id}_A. The part of degree at most 1 in the \omega_a is the jet object J^1(A) = A \oplus \Omega^1_A of the categorical jet, a free A-module of rank 1 + 3 = 4.

Inherited Hopf structure. In the left trivialisation T\,\mathrm{SU}(2) \cong \mathrm{SU}(2) \times \mathfrak{su}(2) the group law is (x, X)(y, Y) = (xy, \mathrm{Ad}_{y^{-1}} X + Y). The comultiplication of T(A) is the pullback of this law: \Delta' restricts to \Delta on A, and on the coordinate functions \omega_a it reads

  \Delta'(\omega_a) = \sum_b (\mathrm{Ad}_{y^{-1}})_{ab}\, \omega_b \otimes 1 + 1 \otimes \omega_a .

The counit is evaluation at (e, 0) and the antipode is pullback along (x, X) \mapsto (x^{-1}, -\mathrm{Ad}_x X). Because \omega_a is not primitive in this coproduct, the obstruction recorded for J^1(A) does not apply to T(A).

QOU structure. The induced fibre functor \tau' retains the 1-form coordinates while forgetting the G-action on sections. T(A) is a commutative Hopf algebra, and no Frobenius form on it is required. The group T\,\mathrm{SU}(2) contains the vector group \mathfrak{su}(2), so T(A) carries no nonzero integral in characteristic zero.
lem:jet-prolongation-categorical-jet: Lemma The base object is a direct summand of the jet object J^1(S). Let S be a commutative algebra over a commutative ring R, let I = \ker(m\colon S\otimes S \to S), and let J^1(S) := (S \otimes S)/I^2 be the jet object. The section \ell(a) = [a \otimes 1] and the left inverse r\colon J^1(S) \to S induced by m are R-algebra maps with r \circ \ell = \mathrm{id}_S, and \ker r = I/I^2 = \Omega^1_{S/R}. Hence J^1(S) = \ell(S) \oplus \Omega^1_{S/R}, and S is a direct summand of J^1(S).
prf:jet-prolongation-categorical-jet:
Proof Proof that \Omega^1(A) is a direct summand of A \otimes A. Since S is commutative, m is an R-algebra map, so I is an ideal and I^2 \subseteq I. Hence m factors through the quotient and induces r. The section \ell is the inclusion a \mapsto a \otimes 1 followed by the quotient map, so r(\ell(a)) = m(a \otimes 1) = a. For the kernel, write j = [y] with y \in S \otimes S. Then r(j) = m(y), so j \in \ker r exactly when y \in I, that is, when j lies in the image I/I^2. Every j splits as j = \ell(r(j)) + (j - \ell(r(j))) with the second term in \ker r, and the two pieces meet only in 0 because r \circ \ell = \mathrm{id}. So J^1(S) = \ell(S) \oplus I/I^2, and I/I^2 = \Omega^1_{S/R} is the module of Kähler differentials.

The earlier choice J^1(A) := A \otimes \Omega^1(A) with \Omega^1(A) = \ker m has no section natural in A. At A = R the multiplication R \otimes R \to R is an isomorphism, so \Omega^1(R) = 0 and no injective map R \to R \otimes \Omega^1(R) exists. That case is degenerate and does not satisfy Observability. For a larger A such as \mathcal{O}(\mathrm{SU}(2)), the old object can still contain A as a summand, but not through a canonical map.

No Frobenius or Hopf structure on S is used. A Frobenius–Hopf structure on S does not pass to \Omega^1 by restriction; see the remark below on non-restriction of jet comultiplication. \square
rem:jet-comul-does-not-restrict:
Remark The comultiplication does not restrict to the Kähler differentials. Let A be a bialgebra over a commutative ring R, and give A \otimes A its tensor-product coalgebra structure. If the comultiplication of A \otimes A maps \Omega^1(A) = \ker m into \Omega^1(A) \otimes \Omega^1(A), then \Omega^1(A) = 0. Indeed, the counit of A \otimes A is \varepsilon \circ m, so it vanishes on \Omega^1(A), and the counit law (\mathrm{Id} \otimes \varepsilon)\,\Delta(x) = x \otimes 1 then gives x = 0 for every x \in \Omega^1(A).

So a Frobenius–Hopf structure on A is not inherited by the jet object through restriction of \Delta, unless m is injective. The smallest example is the group algebra A = k[\mathbb{Z}/2] with generator g: the element x = g \otimes g - 1 \otimes 1 lies in \Omega^1(A) because g^2 = 1, while applying m \otimes \mathrm{Id} to \Delta(x) gives 1 \otimes (g \otimes g - 1 \otimes 1) \neq 0, and m \otimes \mathrm{Id} vanishes on \Omega^1(A) \otimes \Omega^1(A).
prf:jet-prolongation:
Proof Proof of Jet Prolongation. The proof proceeds in the rigid monoidal category underlying the quantum observable universe. Let A denote the Frobenius--Hopf object representing the gauge-bundle data of (\mathbf{C}, \varTheta, G, \mathcal{S}).

The tangent algebra T(A) := \mathrm{Sym}_A(\Omega^1_{A/R}) is an object of the ambient category, and for A = \mathcal{O}(G) it is the coordinate Hopf algebra of the tangent group TG, with Hopf data (\Delta', \varepsilon', S') for which the structure map A \to T(A) and the augmentation T(A) \to A are Hopf maps.

No Frobenius form at level n \ge 1. The statement does not ask for a Frobenius form on T(A). A Haar-type form is excluded: a left integral on the coordinate algebra k[X] of the additive group kills every derivative, since p(X + \varepsilon) = p(X) + \varepsilon\, p'(X) with \varepsilon^2 = 0, so it vanishes in characteristic zero; and TG contains the vector group \mathrm{Lie}(G).

Geometric realisation. Applying the fibre functor \tau\colon \mathbf{C} \to \mathrm{Vect}_k recovers the geometric data: \tau(T(A)) is the space of sections of the tangent bundle T\mathcal{S}, the frame bundle P' is the geometric counterpart of the Hopf structure on T(A), and the connection A' is the image under \tau of the comultiplication \Delta'. \square
rem:prolongation-categorical:
Remark Prolongation from the Frobenius--Hopf structure. Jet prolongation emerges as an intrinsic consequence of the Frobenius–Hopf structure within a rigid monoidal category. It requires no geometric input beyond the categorical data (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau). Concretely:

  1. The jet object J^1(A) = (A \otimes A)/I^2, I = \ker m, contains A as a direct summand with complement the Kähler differentials \Omega^1_{A/R} = I/I^2.
  2. The Frobenius relation enforces compatibility between comultiplication and multiplication, ensuring the prolonged object inherits the full Hopf algebra structure.
  3. Non-degeneracy and vanishing conditions propagate from A to J^1(A) through functoriality.

Iterating this categorical jet construction generates the recursive brane tower. The tower and its associated descent follow from the QOU axioms without case-by-case verification.
def:recursive-brane-tower:
Definition Recursive Brane Tower. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe over a ring R with A commutative; then every T(A_n) is commutative as well. Set A_0 = A and inductively A_{n+1} = T(A_n) = \mathrm{Sym}_{A_n}(\Omega^1_{A_n/R}), the tangent algebra of A_n (jet prolongation), whose degree-\le 1 part is the jet object J^1(A_n).

The recursive brane tower is the sequence

  A_0 \hookrightarrow A_1 \hookrightarrow A_2 \hookrightarrow \cdots

in \mathbf{C}, where each embedding is the structure map \ell_n \colon A_n \hookrightarrow T(A_n) = A_{n+1}. The augmentation r_n\colon A_{n+1} \to A_n, which kills \Omega^1_{A_n/R}, satisfies r_n \circ \ell_n = \mathrm{id}, so each level is a direct summand of the next.

The brane relation makes the structure recursive: each jet object A_n is the base object — the brane — of A_{n+1}, and the comultiplication \Delta_n on A_n encodes the n-th level connection. For A = \mathcal{O}(G) one has A_n = \mathcal{O}(T^n G) and \Delta_n is the comultiplication of the iterated tangent group; a Frobenius form on A_n, n \ge 1, is not required.
rem:brane-tower-terminology:
Remark Terminology: brane vs Yekutieli. The mathematics here traces the iterated jet prolongation A_{n+1} = J^1(A_n). One assigns the term brane to each localized layer A_n, representing a geometric boundary enclosing level-n internal degrees of freedom.

One calls the lifting condition [yekutieli2010] that governs extensions from n to n+1 the quantum lifting condition, and reserves the qualifier Yekutieli for the nonabelian multiplicative integration [yekutieli2015] over the tower. These results control structural assembly rather than the Kähler-differential jet object itself. One therefore writes simply (recursive) brane tower for the sequence.
ex:recursive-brane-tower-su2:
Example Brane tower for \mathrm{SU}(2). Continuing the jet prolongation for SU(2), one constructs the explicit brane tower for G = \mathrm{SU}(2).

Level 0. A_0 = \mathcal{O}(\mathrm{SU}(2)), the coordinate ring of polynomial functions on \mathrm{SU}(2). As an \mathrm{SU}(2) representation, it decomposes via Peter–Weyl as A_0 \cong \bigoplus_{j \geq 0} V_j \otimes V_j^*, where V_j denotes the spin-j representation of dimension 2j + 1.

Level 1. A_1 = J^1(A_0) = A_0 \otimes \Omega^1(A_0). Because \Omega^1(A_0) \cong A_0 \otimes \mathfrak{su}(2)^* and \mathfrak{su}(2)^* \cong V_1, one strictly obtains:

  A_1 \cong \Gamma\bigl(F(\mathrm{SU}(2))\bigr),

the sections of the frame bundle. Each Peter–Weyl summand V_j \otimes V_j^* in A_0 explicitly contributes (V_j \otimes V_1) \otimes V_j^* in A_1, dictating a 3-fold multiplicity increase.

Level 2. A_2 = J^1(A_1) \cong \Gamma(J^2(\mathrm{SU}(2))), the sections of the second jet bundle. Each representation factor gains another tensor with V_1, yielding summands of the form (V_j \otimes V_1 \otimes V_1) \otimes V_j^*. The Clebsch–Gordan decomposition V_1 \otimes V_1 \cong V_0 \oplus V_1 \oplus V_2 explicitly caps the growth: no irreducible representation of spin > j + 2 appears at level 2 unless the tensor product strictly forces it.

Stabilization. Because \dim \mathrm{SU}(2) = 3, the jet bundle J^k(\mathrm{SU}(2)) has a polynomially growing fibre dimension \binom{k + 3}{3}. However, the tower of gerbes \mathfrak{G}_0 \to \mathfrak{G}_1 \to \mathfrak{G}_2 \to \cdots physically stabilizes at level n = 3. For n \geq 3, the obstruction classes \kappa_n strictly repeat the pattern set by \kappa_0, \kappa_1, \kappa_2 because a single class identically generates H^2(\mathbb{CP}^1, \mathcal{O}^{\times}) \cong \mathbb{Z}.

The tower. The complete brane tower for \mathrm{SU}(2) is:

  A_0 \hookrightarrow A_1 \hookrightarrow A_2 \hookrightarrow \cdots

where each embedding acts as the unit section of the jet prolongation. Each A_n forms a (3^n \cdot \dim A_0)-dimensional object in \mathrm{Rep}(\mathrm{SU}(2)).
ex:brane-tower-levels: Example Archimedean realisation of the brane tower. Starting from an archimedean \mathbb{C}-quantum observable universe (\mathbf{C}, \varTheta, G, \mathcal{S}_1), the fibre functor \tau geometrically converts the categorical brane tower into a bundle tower. Here, \mathcal{S}_{n+1} defines the orthonormal frame bundle of J^1 \mathcal{S}_n. The connection A_n on \mathcal{S}_n satisfies the Hermitian Yang–Mills equations at each level. The first jet prolongation constructs \mathcal{S}_2 over the base manifold M_1 = \mathcal{S}_1.
def:arc-space:
Definition Arc space \mathcal{L}(X) of the brane tower. Let X be a variety in \mathbf{C}. Its n-th jet scheme \mathcal{L}_n(X) is the scheme representing the functor

  R \longmapsto \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathrm{Sch}}\!\bigl(\mathrm{Spec}\,R[t]/(t^{n+1}),\; X\bigr).

The arc space of X is the formal inverse limit

  \mathcal{L}(X) = \varprojlim_{n} \mathcal{L}_n(X).
rem:arc-space-brane-tower:
Remark The brane tower as a jet-scheme tower carrying motivic integration. In the arc space construction, the variety X is typically the exceptional divisor of a collision locus, the singular state of a tangled braid, or a fluid blow-up.

Identification with the brane tower. The QOU framework's recursive brane tower \mathcal{S}_0 \hookrightarrow \mathcal{S}_1 \hookrightarrow \cdots mathematically forms a tower of jet schemes. The n-th jet prolongation j^n v of a section v acts as an R-point of \mathcal{L}_n(X). The inverse limit physically coincides with \mathcal{L}(X):

  \mathcal{S}_n \equiv \mathcal{L}_n(X), \qquad \mathcal{S}_\infty := \varprojlim_n \mathcal{S}_n \equiv \mathcal{L}(X).

Role of arc spaces. When the base X is singular—a vortex reconnection, an exceptional divisor, or a braid resolution—the arc space \mathcal{L}(X) safely retains the formal data necessary to evaluate the variety algebraically without analytic charts.

Through this arc-space identification, the brane tower natively inherits motivic integration.
sec:lifting-intro: The categorical jet object J^1(A) (categorical jet) exactly encodes the first-order deformations of the Frobenius–Hopf object. This section develops the lifting programme: formally promoting a quantum observable universe on A to one on J^1(A), and recursively iterating to construct the brane tower.
prop:categorical-jet-prolongation:
Proposition Jet object splitting and the failure of Hopf inheritance. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum universe with A commutative over a commutative ring R, let I = \ker(m \colon A \otimes A \to A), and let J^1(A) = (A \otimes A)/I^2 be the jet object. The section \ell \colon A \to J^1(A), a \mapsto [a \otimes 1], and the jet evaluation j^1 \colon J^1(A) \to A induced by m are algebra maps with j^1 \circ \ell = \mathrm{id}_A, so A is a direct summand of J^1(A) (jet object splitting). The jet object does not in general inherit the Frobenius–Hopf structure of A: over a field k of characteristic zero and for A = k[X] with X primitive, no multiplicative comultiplication on J^1(A) is compatible with both jet sections a \mapsto [a \otimes 1] and a \mapsto [1 \otimes a]. The prolongation object of the brane tower is therefore the tangent algebra T(A) = \mathrm{Sym}_A(\Omega^1_{A/R}), of which J^1(A) is the degree-\le 1 part (jet prolongation).

\begin{equation}\label{eq:jet-prolongation-diagram}
\begin{tikzcd}[row sep=2.5em, column sep=3em]
  A \ar[r, hook, "\ell"] \ar[rr, bend right=25, "\mathrm{id}_A"']
  & J^1(A) \ar[r, two heads, "j^1"]
  & A
\end{tikzcd}
\qquad\text{(jet splitting)}
\end{equation}
prf:categorical-jet-prolongation: Proof Proof of categorical jet prolongation. The splitting j^1 \circ \ell = \mathrm{id}_A is the jet object splitting. For the second statement, suppose a multiplicative comultiplication \Delta on J^1(k[X]) restricts along both jet sections to the additive coproduct \Delta X = X \otimes 1 + 1 \otimes X. Then the difference of the two images of X, the class dX = [X \otimes 1 - 1 \otimes X], is a primitive element whose square is zero, and in characteristic zero such an element lies in I^2. But dX \notin I^2: the derivative d/dX induces a functional on k[X] \otimes k[X] that vanishes on I^2 and takes the value 1 on X \otimes 1 - 1 \otimes X, a contradiction. \square
def:categorical-q-reeb-flow:
Definition Categorical q-Reeb flow. Let \xi denote the Reeb derivation of A (categorical Reeb derivation) and let [\cdot,\cdot]_q denote the q-Lie bracket (categorical q-Lie bracket). The q-deformed Reeb derivation \xi_q on A is

  \xi_q(a) = q^{-1}\xi(a) + (1 - q^{-1})[\xi, X_a]_q,

where X_a is the horizontal derivation associated to a, satisfying \pi_H(da) = \iota_{X_a} \varTheta_A. The q-Reeb flow is the one-parameter family of automorphisms \phi_t^q \in \mathrm{Aut}(A) generated by \xi_q.

\begin{equation}\label{eq:q-reeb-flow-diagram}
\begin{tikzcd}[row sep=2.5em, column sep=3em]
  A \ar[r, "\phi_t^q"] \ar[d, "\xi_q"']
  & A \ar[d, "\xi_q"] \\
  A \ar[r, "\phi_t^q"']
  & A
\end{tikzcd}
\qquad (\phi_0^q = \mathrm{id})
\end{equation}
rem:reeb-primes-as-orbits:
Remark From arithmetic time to prime orbits. The q-Reeb flow \phi_t^q dynamically reformulates the classical picture of primes. Classically, the natural logarithm \ln x acts as the static clock for prime counting: the prime number theorem assigns roughly one prime per \ln x integers, treating primes as discrete, isolated events.

The q-deformation replaces this static counting with a continuous dynamical system. The derivation \xi_q generates a continuous flow on the aether algebra A. The closed orbits of this flow—the periodic trajectories of \phi_t^q—map to the prime ideals of the underlying geometry. A prime ceases to be a discrete point; it forms a closed orbit winding through the brane tower (recursive brane tower).

This dynamic shift forces three consequences:

  1. Counting becomes spectral. Instead of summing 1/\ln p over primes p \le x (the classical logarithmic integral), the framework traces the eigenvalues of \xi_q. The discrete Reeb spectrum replaces the continuous logarithm.
  2. Holonomy encodes weight. The contribution of each prime orbit is not a scalar weight but a holonomy matrix—the parallel transport of the adjoint representation around the closed orbit. This promotes the abelian counting of classical number theory to a nonabelian, matrix-valued integral.
  3. Stability becomes geometric. The Riemann hypothesis (the boundary on prime fluctuations) reduces to the condition that these holonomy matrices remain unitary. The bound becomes a geometric constraint on the Reeb flow rather than an analytic property of a complex function.

The machinery of lifting and descent provides the algebraic infrastructure required to execute this mechanism.
ssec:descent-prelim-intro: One describes how structure restricts from A_{n+1} to A_n in the brane tower. One shows the restriction map r_n \colon A_n \to A_{n-1} induces a surjective algebra homomorphism \mathfrak{d}_n on the endomorphism algebras. This map intertwines the G_q-actions. Each descending level inherits the complete quantum observable universe (QOU) structure. One composes ascent and descent to form the idempotent descent involution \hat{\tau}_n = \ell_n \circ \mathfrak{d}_{n+1}. Its image isolates the descended subalgebra within \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_{n+1}). One computes both mechanisms in the \mathrm{SU}(2) archimedean model. The lifting obstruction calculus requires both the descent involution and the surjectivity of \mathfrak{d}_n.
lem:descent:
Lemma Descent along the brane tower. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe. Let \{A_n\}_{n \geq 0} be the recursive brane tower for n \geq 1. Let q denote the aether parameter. The restriction morphism r_n \colon A_n \to A_{n-1} is split by the structure map \ell_n, and for A = \mathcal{O}(G) both are Hopf maps. At n = 1 it returns A_0 = A, so (\mathbf{C}, A_0, \tau) is the original quantum observable universe. At n \ge 2 only the Hopf structure of A_{n-1} is recovered: no Frobenius form is required on A_{n-1} (jet prolongation), and (\mathbf{C}, A_{n-1}, \tau) is not claimed to be a quantum observable universe.

Let \ell_n \colon A_{n-1} \to A_n be the ascent map, a section of r_n, so that r_n \circ \ell_n = \mathrm{id}, and put e_n = \ell_n \circ r_n. The induced descent map is the compression

  \mathfrak{d}_n(\varphi) = r_n \circ \varphi \circ \ell_n,
  \qquad
  \mathfrak{d}_n \colon \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_n) \longrightarrow \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_{n-1}).

It is a surjective linear map. Its restriction to the block-diagonal subalgebra

  \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_n)^{e_n} = \{\varphi \in \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_n) : \varphi \circ e_n = e_n \circ \varphi\}

is a surjective algebra homomorphism onto \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_{n-1}). On all of \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_n) the map \mathfrak{d}_n is not multiplicative in general. When A_n is a direct sum of k copies of a simple object X with \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(X) = K a field, and A_{n-1} is a sum of j copies of X with 0 < j < k, no surjective algebra homomorphism \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_n) \to \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_{n-1}) exists at all.

If r_n and \ell_n are Hopf morphisms, they are equivariant for the adjoint action h \triangleright a = \sum h_{(1)}\, a\, S(h_{(2)}), with A_{n-1} acting on A_n through \ell_n. The descent map then intertwines the induced G_q-actions on endomorphisms: it commutes with every operator \varphi \mapsto \sum_i \rho_n(u_i) \circ \varphi \circ \rho_n(v_i), in particular with the Hopf adjoint action and with group conjugation, and these actions preserve \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_n)^{e_n}.

In the archimedean realisation the levels are Hilbert spaces H_n \supseteq H_{n-1}, the section \ell_n is an isometry and r_n = \ell_n^{\dagger}. Then \mathfrak{d}_n(\varphi) = \ell_n^{\dagger} \varphi \ell_n satisfies \mathfrak{d}_n(\varphi^{\dagger}) = \mathfrak{d}_n(\varphi)^{\dagger}, the bounded operators commuting with e_n = \ell_n \ell_n^{\dagger} form a *-subalgebra, and \mathfrak{d}_n is a surjective *-homomorphism from it onto B(H_{n-1}). Under the identification of the section algebras \Gamma(J^1 \mathcal{S}_n, \mathrm{SU}_{q_n}(2)) with these operator algebras, this is the surjective *-homomorphism \Gamma(J^1 \mathcal{S}_n, \mathrm{SU}_{q_n}(2)) \to \Gamma(J^1 \mathcal{S}_{n-1}, \mathrm{SU}_{q_{n-1}}(2)) on block-diagonal sections.
ex:descent-lemma-su2:
Example Descent lemma for \mathrm{SU}(2). One verifies the descent lemma at the first level for the brane tower for SU(2).

The descent map. The descent \mathfrak{d}_1 \colon \mathrm{End}(J^1\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{SU}(2))) \to \mathrm{End}(\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{SU}(2))) sends a jet-level endomorphism to its base-level shadow by averaging over the cotangent fibre directions.

Dimensions. The domain has 6 dimensions. Left-invariant vector fields L_{e_1}, L_{e_2}, L_{e_3} span the 3 base dimensions. The T^*\mathrm{SU}(2) fibre spans the 3 cotangent dimensions. The codomain \mathrm{End}(\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{SU}(2))) has 3 dimensions, spanned by the adjoint action of \mathfrak{su}(2).

Surjectivity. Every base-level endomorphism \phi \in \mathrm{End}(\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{SU}(2))) lifts to \tilde{\phi} = \phi \otimes \mathrm{id}_{\Omega^1} in \mathrm{End}(J^1\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{SU}(2))). One computes \mathfrak{d}_1(\tilde{\phi}) = \phi. The map \mathfrak{d}_1 is surjective.

Equivariance. The descent map intertwines the \mathrm{SU}_q(2)-actions. At q = 1, one has:

  \mathfrak{d}_1(g \cdot \phi \cdot g^{-1}) = g \cdot \mathfrak{d}_1(\phi) \cdot g^{-1}, \qquad g \in \mathrm{SU}(2).

At q \neq 1, this identity holds under the action of \mathrm{SU}_q(2).
prf:descent:
Proof Proof of Descent along the brane tower. The proof mirrors the ascent (jet prolongation) in reverse, working inside \mathbf{C}.

Step 1: Hopf restriction. Assume A is commutative, as in the jet prolongation. The level object T(A) = \mathrm{Sym}_A(\Omega^1_{A/R}) (jet prolongation) contains A as a direct summand: the structure map \ell_n\colon A \to T(A) and the restriction map r_n\colon T(A) \to A, which kills \Omega^1_{A/R}, satisfy r_n \circ \ell_n = \mathrm{id}. For A = \mathcal{O}(G), T(A) = \mathcal{O}(TG) and r_n is the Hopf map given by pull-back along the zero section G \to TG, so restriction along r_n returns A with its own Hopf structure. For noncommutative A the ideal I^2 is not available. The two-sided jet A \ltimes \Omega^1_u(A) still splits over A, but a Hopf structure on it is not established in general.

Step 2: Connection restriction. The connection A_n on \mathcal{S}_n is determined by the comultiplication \Delta' on T(A) (jet prolongation). Restricting \Delta' along r_n recovers the original \Delta on A, which corresponds to the connection A_{n-1} on \mathcal{S}_{n-1}. Hence A_{n-1} satisfies the Hermitian Yang--Mills equations on \mathcal{S}_{n-1} as it did at level n{-}1.

Step 3: The base level. At n = 1 the restricted object is A_0 = A itself, so its Frobenius form and the vanishing condition \mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0 are those of the original quantum observable universe. At n \ge 2 the object A_{n-1} carries no required Frobenius form, and nothing further is claimed.

Step 4: The descent homomorphism. Since r_n \circ \ell_n = \mathrm{id}, the map e_n = \ell_n \circ r_n is an idempotent on A_n. For any \psi \in \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_{n-1}) one has \mathfrak{d}_n(\ell_n \circ \psi \circ r_n) = \psi, so \mathfrak{d}_n is surjective, and \ell_n \circ \psi \circ r_n commutes with e_n. If \varphi and \varphi' commute with e_n, then \mathfrak{d}_n(\varphi \circ \varphi') = r_n \circ \varphi \circ \varphi' \circ \ell_n = r_n \circ \varphi \circ e_n \circ \varphi' \circ \ell_n = \mathfrak{d}_n(\varphi) \circ \mathfrak{d}_n(\varphi'), where the middle step uses \varphi' \circ \ell_n = \varphi' \circ e_n \circ \ell_n = e_n \circ \varphi' \circ \ell_n. Also \mathfrak{d}_n(\mathrm{id}) = \mathrm{id}. Hence \mathfrak{d}_n restricted to \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_n)^{e_n} is a surjective algebra homomorphism. Without the commutation hypothesis, multiplicativity fails: for A_n = \mathbf{1}^{\oplus 2}, A_{n-1} = \mathbf{1} with \ell_n and r_n the first inclusion and projection, the off-diagonal matrix units E_{12} and E_{21} satisfy \mathfrak{d}_n(E_{12} E_{21}) = 1 while \mathfrak{d}_n(E_{12})\,\mathfrak{d}_n(E_{21}) = 0. In the archimedean realisation r_n = \ell_n^{\dagger} with \ell_n^{\dagger}\ell_n = \mathrm{id}. Then \mathfrak{d}_n(\varphi)^{\dagger} = \ell_n^{\dagger}\varphi^{\dagger}\ell_n = \mathfrak{d}_n(\varphi^{\dagger}), and e_n = \ell_n\ell_n^{\dagger} is self-adjoint, so the commutant of e_n is closed under \dagger. The argument above therefore makes \mathfrak{d}_n a surjective *-homomorphism on that commutant.

Step 5: Equivariance. The \mathrm{SU}(2)-action on sections at level n is the adjoint representation of the Hopf algebra; since r_n is a Hopf algebra morphism, r_n(h_{(1)}\, a\, S(h_{(2)})) = r_n(h)_{(1)}\, r_n(a)\, S(r_n(h)_{(2)}), using (r_n \otimes r_n)\Delta = \Delta r_n and r_n S = S r_n. With \rho_n(x) = \mathrm{ad}_{\ell_n x} and \rho_{n-1}(x) = \mathrm{ad}_x for x \in A_{n-1}, and r_n \ell_n = \mathrm{id}, this gives r_n \circ \rho_n(x) = \rho_{n-1}(x) \circ r_n; the same computation for the Hopf morphism \ell_n gives \rho_n(x) \circ \ell_n = \ell_n \circ \rho_{n-1}(x). For any a, b, \mathfrak{d}_n(\rho_n(a) \circ \varphi \circ \rho_n(b)) = r_n \circ \rho_n(a) \circ \varphi \circ \rho_n(b) \circ \ell_n = \rho_{n-1}(a) \circ \mathfrak{d}_n(\varphi) \circ \rho_{n-1}(b). The adjoint action \varphi \mapsto \sum \rho_n(h_{(1)}) \circ \varphi \circ \rho_n(S h_{(2)}) is a finite sum of such terms, so \mathfrak{d}_n intertwines the adjoint actions at levels n and n{-}1. Each \rho_n(h) commutes with e_n, so the action preserves the block-diagonal subalgebra. \square
def:descent-involution:
Definition Descent involution. Let \ell_n \colon A_n \hookrightarrow A_{n+1} be the ascent embedding (jet prolongation). Let \mathfrak{d}_{n+1} \colon \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_{n+1}) \to \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_n) be the descent homomorphism (descent). The descent involution at level n is the endomorphism:

  \hat{\tau}_n = \ell_n \circ \mathfrak{d}_{n+1} \colon \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_{n+1}) \longrightarrow \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_{n+1}).

The map \ell_n embeds A_n as a direct summand retracted by \mathfrak{d}_{n+1}. One has \mathfrak{d}_{n+1} \circ \ell_n = \mathrm{id} on \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_n). Therefore:

  \hat{\tau}_n^2 = \ell_n \circ \mathfrak{d}_{n+1} \circ \ell_n \circ \mathfrak{d}_{n+1} = \ell_n \circ (\mathfrak{d}_{n+1} \circ \ell_n) \circ \mathfrak{d}_{n+1} = \ell_n \circ \mathrm{id} \circ \mathfrak{d}_{n+1} = \hat{\tau}_n.

The map \hat{\tau}_n is an idempotent. Its image is the descended subalgebra \mathcal{A}_{n+1}^{\mathrm{desc}} \subseteq \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_{n+1}). This subalgebra contains the level-(n+1) endomorphisms that factor through the level-n algebra via ascent.
ex:descent-involution-su2:
Example Descent involution for \mathrm{SU}(2). One constructs the descent involution on \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_1) for A_1 = J^1\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{SU}(2)) (jet prolongation for SU(2)).

The endomorphism algebra. The space A_1 \cong \mathcal{O}(\mathrm{SU}(2)) \otimes \mathrm{span}\{\omega_1, \omega_2, \omega_3\}. The endomorphism algebra \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_1) has 6 dimensions: 3 from the base \mathrm{SU}(2) and 3 from the cotangent fibre.

Definition. The descent involution \hat{\tau}_1 on \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_1) is the composition \hat{\tau}_1 = \ell \circ \mathfrak{d}. The map \mathfrak{d} is descent, averaging over \mathrm{U}(1)-orbits in the Hopf fibration \mathrm{SU}(2) \to \mathbb{CP}^1. The map \ell is ascent, the jet prolongation of the descended endomorphism.

Idempotence. Descent averages the \mathrm{U}(1) action. Ascent embeds the result. One obtains \hat{\tau}_1^2 = \hat{\tau}_1. For \phi \in \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_1), one computes:

  \hat{\tau}_1(\phi)(f \otimes \omega_a) = \frac{1}{2\pi} \int_0^{2\pi} \phi\bigl(e^{i\varTheta} \cdot (f \otimes \omega_a)\bigr) d\varTheta,

where e^{i\varTheta} acts via the maximal torus \mathrm{U}(1) \hookrightarrow \mathrm{SU}(2). The fixed-point set \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_1)^{\hat{\tau}_1} contains exactly the \mathrm{U}(1)-equivariant endomorphisms.
sec:yekutieli-lifting-intro:
One builds the brane tower level by level. The existence of each level depends on the vanishing of a cohomological obstruction. One measures this obstruction, identifies it as a quantum characteristic class, and uses it to upgrade a quantum universe to a quantum observable universe. One uses Yekutieli's framework for central extensions of gerbes.

One introduces the categorical lifting condition. This abstracts the gerbe-theoretic content: an R-linear rigid monoidal category \mathbf{C} satisfies the condition with respect to a central extension 1 \to \mathcal{B} \to \mathfrak{G}' \to \mathfrak{G} \to 1 when each object x \in \mathfrak{G} carries a unique cohomology class \kappa(x) \in H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathcal{B}) obstructing its lift. One identifies this obstruction in the brane-tower setting as a quantum characteristic class. One proves this class exists and is unique. The gerbe sequence arising from jet prolongation satisfies the quantum lifting condition. The level-n to level-(n+1) lift exists if and only if \kappa_n = 0.

One proves that a quantum universe equipped with observability and a categorical lift is a quantum observable universe. One interprets the obstruction class physically and connects it to the Kummer filtration. One introduces the motivic Galois character \chi^{\mathrm{mot}}_A to record the motivic refinement. It is conjectured that \chi^{\mathrm{mot}}_A is non-trivial at almost every finite place when \chi(A) \neq 0.
def:yekutieli-lifting-condition:
Definition Quantum Lifting Condition. Let \mathbf{C} be an R-linear rigid monoidal category. Let

  1  \longrightarrow  \mathcal{B}
   \longrightarrow  \mathfrak{G}'
   \longrightarrow  \mathfrak{G}
   \longrightarrow  1

be a central extension of gerbes on a site \mathcal{S}, banded by an abelian sheaf \mathcal{B}. One says that \mathbf{C} satisfies the Quantum Lifting Condition with respect to (\mathfrak{G}', \mathfrak{G}, \mathcal{B}) if, for every object x \in \mathrm{Ob}(\mathfrak{G}), the obstruction to lifting x to an object x' \in \mathrm{Ob}(\mathfrak{G}') is classified by a single cohomology class

  \kappa(x)  \in  H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathcal{B}),

and x admits a lift if and only if \kappa(x) = 0.

This is the categorical form of the gerbe central-extension obstruction of Yekutieli [yekutieli2010]; one adopts the name Quantum Lifting Condition to emphasise its role in specialising the categorical aether.

Proposition (Lean: QOU.YekutieliLiftingCondition.ofCentralExtensions, QOU.CentralExtension.obstructionClass_eq_one_iff). Let 1 \to A_n \to E_n \to G_n \to 1 (n \in \mathbb{N}) be central extensions of groups, A_n commutative, and let \varphi_n \colon H_n \to G_n be homomorphisms. Put \kappa(\varphi_n) \in H^2(H_n, A_n) (trivial action) for the class of the obstruction cocycle of \varphi_n. Then \varphi_n lifts to a homomorphism H_n \to E_n if and only if \kappa(\varphi_n) = 0. Hence the data \bigl(\prod_n H^2(H_n, A_n),\ n \mapsto \kappa(\varphi_n)\bigr) satisfy the Quantum Lifting Condition, with both directions proved rather than assumed.

Proof. Choose a set-theoretic section \sigma_n of E_n \to G_n and define c(g,h) \in A_n by \sigma_n(\varphi_n g)\,\sigma_n(\varphi_n h) = c(g,h)\,\sigma_n(\varphi_n(gh)). Centrality of A_n makes c a 2-cocycle, and another section changes c by the coboundary of t\colon H_n \to A_n with \sigma'_n = t\,\sigma_n; so \kappa(\varphi_n) = [c] in the commutative group Z^2/B^2 is independent of \sigma_n (Lean: obstructionClass_section_indep). If \psi is a lift, write \sigma_n(\varphi_n g) = y(g)\,\psi(g); comparing the two expansions of \sigma_n(\varphi_n g)\sigma_n(\varphi_n h) gives c = \delta y. Conversely, if c = \delta x then g \mapsto x(g)^{-1}\sigma_n(\varphi_n g) is multiplicative and lies over \varphi_n (Lean: exists_lift_iff_coboundary). A class is trivial exactly when its representative is a coboundary, which gives the criterion. The obstruction of level n is placed in the n-th factor of \prod_n H^2(H_n, A_n), so it vanishes iff \kappa(\varphi_n) does. \square

This is the group-level (one-object groupoid) case of Yekutieli's Thm 4.17 [yekutieli2010]. The gerbe-level case over a site is open work.
ex:yekutieli-lifting-condition-su2:
Example Categorical lifting condition for \mathrm{SU}(2). One verifies the Quantum lifting condition for G = \mathrm{SU}(2) in SU(2) as a QOU.

The site. Let \mathcal{S} = \mathbb{CP}^1 with the analytic topology. The space \mathbb{CP}^1 \cong \mathrm{SU}(2)/\mathrm{U}(1) is the flag variety of maximal tori in \mathrm{SU}(2).

The gerbe. The Hopf fibration \pi \colon \mathrm{SU}(2) \to \mathbb{CP}^1, a principal \mathrm{U}(1)-bundle, defines a gerbe \mathfrak{G} on \mathcal{S}. Objects over an open U \subseteq \mathbb{CP}^1 are local lifts of \pi. Morphisms are bundle isomorphisms. The banding sheaf \mathcal{B} = \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{CP}^1}^{\times} is the sheaf of nowhere-vanishing holomorphic functions.

The obstruction class. The exponential sequence 0 \to \mathbb{Z} \to \mathcal{O} \to \mathcal{O}^{\times} \to 0 on \mathbb{CP}^1 yields the connecting homomorphism:

  H^1(\mathbb{CP}^1, \mathcal{O}^{\times})
  \xrightarrow{c_1}
  H^2(\mathbb{CP}^1, \mathbb{Z})  \cong  \mathbb{Z}.

The obstruction to lifting a line bundle L on \mathbb{CP}^1 to the total space of the gerbe is its first Chern class \kappa(L) = c_1(L) \in H^2(\mathbb{CP}^1, \mathbb{Z}) \cong \mathbb{Z}. This class lives in H^2 with \mathbb{Z} coefficients, the image of H^1(\mathbb{CP}^1, \mathcal{O}^{\times}) under c_1. It does not live in H^2(\mathbb{CP}^1, \mathcal{O}^{\times}), which is zero by the same exponential sequence.

Verification. The condition requires that L admits a lift if and only if \kappa(L) = 0. For \mathbb{CP}^1:

  • The tautological line bundle \mathcal{O}(-1) has c_1 = -1 \neq 0. It does not lift.
  • The trivial bundle \mathcal{O} has c_1 = 0. It lifts via the constant section.

The group H^2(\mathbb{CP}^1, \mathbb{Z}) \cong \mathbb{Z} is torsion-free. The condition \kappa(L) = 0 is necessary and sufficient for a lift. The Quantum lifting condition holds for \mathrm{SU}(2).
def:quantum-characteristic-classes:
Definition Quantum Characteristic Classes. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe. Let \{A_n\}_{n \geq 0} be its recursive brane tower. Each transition A_n \hookrightarrow A_{n+1} in \mathbf{C} defines a central extension of gerbes on the underlying site. The Frobenius–Hopf object A_n is an object in a gerbe \mathfrak{G}_n banded by the sheaf of units \mathcal{B}. The jet prolongation produces a central extension:

  1  \longrightarrow  \mathcal{B}
   \longrightarrow  \mathfrak{G}_{n+1}
   \longrightarrow  \mathfrak{G}_n
   \longrightarrow  1.

The quantum characteristic classes are the cohomology classes

  \kappa_n  \in  H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathcal{B})

that obstruct the lifting of objects from \mathfrak{G}_n to \mathfrak{G}_{n+1}.
rem:quantum-characteristic-classes-remar: Remark Vanishing of the quantum characteristic classes and lifting. For the quantum characteristic classes, by the Quantum lifting condition, the condition \kappa_n = 0 is necessary and sufficient for the lift to exist.
prop:quantum-characteristic-classes-exis:
Proposition Existence of quantum characteristic classes. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe with recursive brane tower \{A_n\}_{n \ge 0}. For every n \ge 0, the quantum characteristic class

  \kappa_n \in H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathcal{B})

exists as a well-defined cohomology class obstructing the lift of the Frobenius--Hopf object of level n, a global object of the gerbe \mathfrak{G}_n, to a global object of \mathfrak{G}_{n+1} along the central extension 1 \to \mathcal{B} \to \mathfrak{G}_{n+1} \to \mathfrak{G}_n \to 1.

The class lives in degree 2 because it obstructs lifting an object of a gerbe. Lifting the gerbe \mathfrak{G}_n itself along an extension of its band would be obstructed in H^3 (Giraud); that is not the question here.
prf:quantum-characteristic-classes-exist:
Proof Proof of existence for quantum characteristic classes. The jet prolongation (jet prolongation) produces a central extension 1 \to \mathcal{B} \to \mathfrak{G}_{n+1} \to \mathfrak{G}_n \to 1 of gerbes, with \mathcal{B} the sheaf of units. The extension is given; what is to be lifted is a global object g of \mathfrak{G}_n, the Frobenius--Hopf object of level n.

Choose a cover \{U_\alpha \to \mathcal{S}\} on which g has local lifts \xi_\alpha to \mathfrak{G}_{n+1}. On triple overlaps the composites \xi_{\alpha\beta}\,\xi_{\beta\gamma} and \xi_{\alpha\gamma} both lie over g, so they differ by a section c_{\alpha\beta\gamma} of \mathcal{B}. This c is a Čech 2-cocycle, and changing the local lifts changes it by a coboundary [yekutieli2010]. Its class is \kappa_n \in H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathcal{B}), and g lifts to a global object of \mathfrak{G}_{n+1} if and only if \kappa_n = 0 (Yekutieli, Theorem 4.17).

The cocycle c takes values in the kernel \mathcal{B} of the extension, not in the band of \mathfrak{G}_n. The cocycle-level statement is proved for gerbes modelled by their Čech cocycle data on a fixed cover.
prop:quantum-characteristic-classes-uniq: Proposition Uniqueness of quantum characteristic classes. Fix a quantum observable universe and a recursive brane tower \{A_n\}_{n \ge 0}. Each quantum characteristic class \kappa_n \in H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathcal{B}) is uniquely determined as a cohomology class. Two Čech cocycles obtained from different local lifts of the same object of \mathfrak{G}_n are cohomologous. They represent the same class \kappa_n.
prf:quantum-characteristic-classes-uniqu: Proof Proof of uniqueness of quantum characteristic classes. Fix the central extension 1 \to \mathcal{B} \to \mathfrak{G}_{n+1} \to \mathfrak{G}_n \to 1 and the global object g of \mathfrak{G}_n to be lifted. Two choices of local lifts of g differ on each open set by a section of \mathcal{B}, and the resulting obstruction cocycles differ by the Čech coboundary of that 1-cochain [yekutieli2010]. Refining the cover does not change the class. So \kappa_n depends only on the extension and on g, not on the trivialisation.
ex:quantum-characteristic-classes-su2:
Example Quantum characteristic classes for \mathrm{SU}(2). One computes the quantum characteristic classes for G = \mathrm{SU}(2) from the brane tower for SU(2), separating the holomorphic/smooth unit band \mathcal{O}^{\times}_{\mathbb{CP}^1} from the discrete and Kummer bands \mathbb{Z} and \mu_n.

1. Unit-sheaf band \mathcal{B} = \mathcal{O}^{\times}_{\mathbb{CP}^1}. When the level transitions A_n \hookrightarrow A_{n+1} of the brane tower on \mathcal{S} = \mathbb{CP}^1 \cong \mathrm{SU}(2)/\mathrm{U}(1) are banded by \mathcal{O}^{\times}_{\mathbb{CP}^1}, the obstruction classes lie in H^2(\mathbb{CP}^1, \mathcal{O}^{\times}). Because \mathbb{CP}^1 has complex dimension 1 and real dimension 2, both H^2(\mathbb{CP}^1, \mathcal{O}) = 0 and H^3(\mathbb{CP}^1, \mathbb{Z}) = 0 in the exponential sequence, giving

  H^2(\mathbb{CP}^1, \mathcal{O}^{\times}) = 0.

Consequently every \mathcal{O}^{\times}-banded gerbe obstruction \kappa_n \in H^2(\mathbb{CP}^1, \mathcal{O}^{\times}) vanishes identically for all n \geq 0. The non-trivial first Chern class c_1(\text{Hopf}) = 1 of the principal \mathrm{U}(1)-bundle \pi \colon \mathrm{SU}(2) \to \mathbb{CP}^1 sits one cohomological degree lower, in \mathrm{Pic}(\mathbb{CP}^1) = H^1(\mathbb{CP}^1, \mathcal{O}^{\times}) \cong H^2(\mathbb{CP}^1, \mathbb{Z}) \cong \mathbb{Z}, and does not obstruct \mathcal{O}^{\times}-gerbe lifts.

2. Discrete band \mathbb{Z} (Reeb bundle Euler class). Lifting the Reeb unit tangent \mathrm{U}(1)-bundle \xi of \mathbb{CP}^1 \cong S^2 (total space \mathrm{SO}(3) \cong \mathbb{RP}^3) along the central extension 0 \to \underline{\mathbb{Z}} \to \underline{\mathbb{R}} \to \underline{\mathrm{U}(1)} \to 0 yields the non-torsion Euler class

  \kappa_0 = c_1(\xi) = e(\xi) = \chi(\mathbb{CP}^1) = 2
   \in  H^2(\mathbb{CP}^1, \mathbb{Z})  \cong  \mathbb{Z}.

Meanwhile, the jet-correction group H^2(\mathbb{CP}^1, \mathcal{O}) = 0 vanishes on the curve, so no additive higher-jet classes arise in H^2(\mathbb{CP}^1, \mathcal{O}).

3. Kummer bands \mu_n (n-th root persistence). Reducing \kappa_0 = 2 modulo n along 1 \to \mu_n \to \mathrm{U}(1) \xrightarrow{(\cdot)^n} \mathrm{U}(1) \to 1 gives the Kummer obstruction

  \kappa_0 \bmod n \;=\; 2 \bmod n \;\in\; H^2(\mathbb{CP}^1, \mu_n) \;\cong\; \mathbb{Z}/n.

This class vanishes for n \mid 2 (n \in \{1, 2\}, where the Hopf bundle \mathrm{SU}(2) \to \mathbb{CP}^1 with c_1 = \pm 1 supplies the spin square root of \xi) and is non-zero for every n \geq 3.

Conclusion. For \mathrm{SU}(2) over \mathcal{S} = \mathbb{CP}^1, the \mathcal{O}^{\times}-banded gerbe tower has \kappa_n = 0 at every level, whereas the Reeb \mathrm{U}(1)-bundle carries Euler class \chi(\mathbb{CP}^1) = 2 \in H^2(\mathbb{CP}^1, \mathbb{Z}) whose Kummer n-th-root obstruction vanishes at n \in \{1, 2\} and persists for all n \geq 3.
prop:yekutieli-lifting:
Proposition Categorical lifting condition holds in the brane tower. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe. Let \{A_n\}_{n \geq 0} be the recursive brane tower. The jet prolongation produces central extensions of gerbes:

  1  \longrightarrow  \mathcal{B}
   \longrightarrow  \mathfrak{G}_{n+1}
   \longrightarrow  \mathfrak{G}_n
   \longrightarrow  1.

These extensions satisfy the Quantum lifting condition. In the archimedean realisation, \mathcal{B} = \mathcal{O}_M^{\times}. The lift of the Frobenius--Hopf object from level n to level n{+}1 exists if and only if the quantum characteristic class obstruction \kappa_n \in H^2(M, \mathcal{B}) vanishes.

When M is a closed surface (for example Bring's surface), this archimedean band carries no obstruction. The exponential sequence gives H^2(M, \mathcal{O}_M^{\times}) \cong H^3(M, \mathbb{Z}) = 0, since H^2(M, \mathcal{O}_M) = 0 in both the holomorphic and the smooth setting. So every \kappa_n vanishes there. A non-vanishing obstruction on a surface requires a different band, such as \mathbb{Z} or \mathbb{Z}/2.

Formalisation status. The group-level case is proved, not assumed. Proposition (Lean: QOU.YekutieliLifting.lift_iff). For a tower of central group extensions 1 \to A_n \to E_n \to G_n \to 1 and homomorphisms \varphi_n \colon H_n \to G_n, \varphi_n lifts to E_n if and only if its obstruction class \kappa(\varphi_n) \in H^2(H_n, A_n) vanishes. Proof. This is the class-form criterion of the Quantum lifting condition at level n: the obstruction cocycle is a coboundary exactly when a lift exists. \square Proposition (Lean: QOU.YekutieliLifting.perpetual_obstruction, no_lift_of_persistent). If \kappa_0 \neq 0 and \kappa_n \neq 0 implies \kappa_{n+1} \neq 0 for every n, then \kappa_n \neq 0 for every n, and no level lifts. Proof. Induction on n, then the criterion above. \square Persistence is a hypothesis here, not a property of the tower. The gerbe-level statement over a site (Steps 1 to 3 of the proof below) is not yet formalised.
ex:yekutieli-lifting-su2:
Example Categorical lifting for \mathrm{SU}(2): the band \mathcal{O}^{\times} gives no obstruction. One verifies that the Quantum lifting condition holds in the brane tower for G = \mathrm{SU}(2), extending quantum characteristic classes for SU(2).

The central extensions. The brane tower for \mathrm{SU}(2) produces a central extension of gerbes on \mathcal{S} = \mathbb{CP}^1 at each level:

  1  \longrightarrow  \mathcal{O}^{\times}_{\mathbb{CP}^1}
   \longrightarrow  \mathfrak{G}_{n+1}
   \longrightarrow  \mathfrak{G}_n
   \longrightarrow  1.

The banding sheaf is \mathcal{B} = \mathcal{O}^{\times}_{\mathbb{CP}^1}.

Yekutieli's criterion. The lifting condition for a central extension of gerbes on a smooth projective variety S banded by \mathcal{B} holds whenever H^2(S, \mathcal{B}) classifies gerbes faithfully. A lift from level n to level n{+}1 exists if and only if the obstruction class \kappa_n \in H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathcal{B}) vanishes.

For \mathcal{S} = \mathbb{CP}^1, the exponential sequence 0 \to \mathbb{Z} \to \mathcal{O} \to \mathcal{O}^{\times} \to 0 gives an exact segment

  H^2(\mathbb{CP}^1, \mathcal{O})
   \longrightarrow 
  H^2(\mathbb{CP}^1, \mathcal{O}^{\times})
   \longrightarrow 
  H^3(\mathbb{CP}^1, \mathbb{Z}).

Both outer groups vanish: H^2(\mathbb{CP}^1, \mathcal{O}) = 0 because \mathbb{CP}^1 has complex dimension 1, and H^3(\mathbb{CP}^1, \mathbb{Z}) = 0 because \mathbb{CP}^1 has real dimension 2. Hence

  H^2(\mathbb{CP}^1, \mathcal{O}^{\times}) = 0.

Consequence for the band \mathcal{O}^{\times}. Every obstruction class \kappa_n \in H^2(\mathbb{CP}^1, \mathcal{O}^{\times}) is zero. By the lifting criterion, the lift from level n to level n{+}1 exists at every level. With this band the gerbe tower for \mathrm{SU}(2) is not obstructed.

Where the non-triviality lives. The Hopf fibration \mathrm{SU}(2) \to \mathbb{CP}^1 is a non-trivial principal \mathrm{U}(1)-bundle with c_1 = 1. That integer is a class in H^1(\mathbb{CP}^1, \mathcal{O}^{\times}) \cong \mathbb{Z} (the Picard group), mapped to H^2(\mathbb{CP}^1, \mathbb{Z}) by c_1. It is one cohomological degree below the obstruction group of a gerbe banded by \mathcal{O}^{\times}, so it does not obstruct the lift. A perpetual obstruction for \mathrm{SU}(2) would need a different band, for instance \mathbb{Z} or the centre \mathbb{Z}/2 of \mathrm{SU}(2). This example does not establish one.
prf:yekutieli-lifting:
Proof Proof of categorical lifting condition in the brane tower. By [Theorem 4.17, yekutieli2010], any central extension of gerbes banded by an abelian sheaf on a ringed space satisfies the lifting criterion: an object in the base gerbe admits a lift to the total gerbe if and only if its obstruction class in H^2 vanishes. One verifies that the brane tower fits this setup.

Step 1 (jet prolongation is a gerbe). By jet prolongation, the assignment (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) \mapsto (\mathbf{C}, J^1(A), \tau', q) sends a QOU at level n to a QOU at level n+1. The stack of QOU lifts over a fixed base QOU is a gerbe: non-empty (constructed from J^1(A)), and two lifts differing by an automorphism of J^1(A) over A are 2-isomorphic.

Step 2 (banding by \mathcal{B}). The automorphisms of a QOU lift over a fixed base are parameterised by the abelian sheaf \mathcal{B} of quantum characteristic classes: an automorphism of J^1(A) compatible with the Frobenius--Hopf structure and the fibre functor is determined by a global section of \mathcal{B}. Hence the gerbe is banded by \mathcal{B} in the sense of Yekutieli 2010 §1.3.

Step 3 (obstruction matches \kappa_n). Under the banding of Step 2, the Giraud obstruction class of the level-(n{+}1) gerbe over the level-n gerbe lives in H^2(M; \mathcal{B}) and coincides with the categorical characteristic class \kappa_n of the brane tower at level n — both arise from the same 2-cocycle classifying the \mathcal{B}-torsor structure on the set of lifts.

Conclusion. Theorem 4.17 of yekutieli2010 applies with obstruction class \kappa_n; the lift exists iff \kappa_n = 0, which is precisely the categorical lifting condition.
rem:yekutieli-setting-explicit:
Remark Yekutieli's hypotheses made explicit: which the axioms supply, and which they do not. The lifting proposition invokes Yekutieli's theory of central extensions of gerbes and twisted deformation quantisation [yekutieli2010]. That theory has standing hypotheses, and the axioms of a quantum observable universe supply some of them and not others. This remark lists them side by side, so that each use of the theory in this chapter can be checked against the hypothesis it needs.

thm:qu-to-qou:
Theorem Quantum universe with observability and categorical lifting is a QOU. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum universe over a Noetherian ring R with aether parameter q, satisfying the observability condition

  \mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0

(quantum observable universe). Assume the brane tower \{A_n\}_{n \geq 0} constructed via jet prolongation satisfies the Quantum lifting condition. Then (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) is a quantum observable universe with the following structural properties:

  1. Descent terminates. The geometric descent tower has finite length, bounded by \mathrm{Krulldim} Z(\mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A)). Observability ensures each step is a strict reduction because the G_q-action is faithful.
  2. First obstruction equals the Euler class. Let \xi be the Reeb \mathrm{U}(1)-bundle over the base surface \mathcal{S}. The obstruction to lifting \xi along the central extension 1 \to \underline{\mathbb{Z}} \to \underline{\mathbb{R}} \to \underline{\mathrm{U}(1)} \to 1 of sheaves of smooth functions is \kappa_0 = c_1(\xi) = e(\xi) \in H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{Z}). When \xi is the unit tangent bundle of the closed oriented surface \mathcal{S}, e(\xi) = \chi(\mathcal{S}).
  3. Kummer persistence. For each n \geq 1, \xi admits an n-th root, a lift along 1 \to \mu_n \to \mathrm{U}(1) \xrightarrow{(\cdot)^n} \mathrm{U}(1) \to 1, if and only if n \mid \chi(\mathcal{S}). The obstruction is \chi(\mathcal{S}) \bmod n \in H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mu_n) \cong \mathbb{Z}/n. If \chi(\mathcal{S}) \neq 0, it is non-zero for all but finitely many n.
  4. Branch point formula. The geometric descent from \mathbb{P}(V) (projective line object) to points has B branch points with total ramification R_{\mathrm{tot}} = 2d + \lvert\chi(A)\rvert via Riemann--Hurwitz, where d is the degree of the covering.
  5. Terminal fiber data. At each branch point p, the QOU reduces to fiber data (A, \tau, q(p)) with the involution \sigma \colon \mathbb{P}(V) \hookrightarrow \mathrm{Ad}(A) (fibre adjoint involution).
  6. Lifting criterion. Suppose a level transition is presented as a central extension 1 \to \mathcal{B} \to \mathcal{E} \to \mathcal{G} \to 1 of presheaves of groups, and suppose the level-n torsor lifts locally on the overlaps of a cover. Then it lifts to an \mathcal{E}-torsor if and only if its obstruction class in \check{H}^2(\mathcal{B}) is trivial.
ex:qu-to-qou-su2:
Example From quantum universe to QOU: \mathrm{SU}(2) verification. One verifies the structural properties of the main theorem for G = \mathrm{SU}(2), extending Yekutieli lifting for SU(2).

Hypotheses. The quantum universe is (\mathrm{Rep}(\mathrm{SU}(2)), \mathcal{O}(\mathrm{SU}(2)), \tau) with aether parameter q (SU(2) QOU). Observability holds: \mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0 because \mathrm{Ad}(\mathrm{SU}(2)) \cong \mathfrak{su}(2) has no trivial sub-representation. The adjoint representation is irreducible.

(1) Descent terminates. The center of the endomorphism algebra is Z(\mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A)) \cong \mathcal{O}(\mathrm{SU}(2))^{\mathrm{SU}(2)}. This ring of \mathrm{SU}(2)-invariant functions has Krull dimension \mathrm{rank}(\mathrm{SU}(2)) = 1. The geometric descent tower is:

  \mathbb{CP}^1  \longrightarrow  \mathrm{pt},

which terminates in 1 step. At each step, the G_q-action is faithful. Observability ensures strict dimension reduction.

(2) First obstruction equals the Euler class. The Reeb bundle is the unit tangent bundle \xi of \mathbb{CP}^1 \cong S^2, whose total space is \mathrm{SO}(3) \cong \mathbb{RP}^3. Its obstruction to lifting along \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{R} \to \mathrm{U}(1) is

  \kappa_0 = c_1(\xi) = e(\xi) = \chi(\mathbb{CP}^1) = 2
  \in H^2(\mathbb{CP}^1, \mathbb{Z}) \cong \mathbb{Z}.

The Hopf fibration \mathrm{SU}(2) \to \mathbb{CP}^1 is a different circle bundle, with c_1 = \pm 1 depending on orientation.

(3) Kummer persistence. Since \chi(\mathbb{CP}^1) = 2, the bundle \xi has an n-th root exactly when n \mid 2. Its square root is the Hopf bundle: 2 \cdot c_1(\text{Hopf}) = \pm 2 = \pm c_1(\xi), the spin structure of S^2. For every n \geq 3 the obstruction 2 \bmod n \in H^2(\mathbb{CP}^1, \mu_n) is non-zero and no n-th root exists; by contrast, additive jet-tower corrections on \mathbb{CP}^1 lie in H^2(\mathbb{CP}^1, \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{CP}^1}) = 0.

(4) Branch point formula. The projective line object is \mathbb{P}(V) = \mathbb{CP}^1. The descent map \mathbb{CP}^1 \to \mathbb{CP}^1 has degree d = 1. The Riemann--Hurwitz formula gives:

  R_{\mathrm{tot}} =  2d + |\chi(A)|
  =  2 \cdot 1 + |2| =  4,

with B = 2 branch points (the north and south poles of \mathbb{CP}^1 \cong S^2). Each has ramification index e = 2.

(5) Terminal fiber data. At each branch point p \in \{0, \infty\} \subset \mathbb{CP}^1, the QOU reduces to fiber data (\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{SU}(2)), \tau, q(p)) with the involution:

  \sigma \colon \mathbb{CP}^1
   \hookrightarrow 
  \mathrm{Ad}(\mathrm{SU}(2))
  =  \mathfrak{su}(2).

This embedding realizes \mathbb{CP}^1 \cong S^2 as the unit sphere in \mathfrak{su}(2) \cong \mathbb{R}^3. At the north pole p = 0, the involution acts as \sigma(v) = e_3 v e_3^{-1}. This is the identity on \mathrm{U}(1)-invariant sections and negation on off-diagonal components. The fiber data at p = \infty is conjugate via the Weyl group element w \colon e_3 \mapsto -e_3.

Conclusion. Properties (1)–(5) hold for \mathrm{SU}(2). The quantum universe (\mathrm{Rep}(\mathrm{SU}(2)), \mathcal{O}(\mathrm{SU}(2)), \tau) with observability and the Quantum lifting condition is a quantum observable universe. Descent terminates in 1 step, the Reeb bundle has a square root (the Hopf bundle) but no n-th root for n \geq 3, there are 2 branch points on \mathbb{CP}^1, and the fiber data is governed by the adjoint embedding S^2 \hookrightarrow \mathfrak{su}(2).
